ai.title: OpenAI launches Dots, its Muse competitor
ai.brief: Dots are always-on AI assistants that OpenAI says can ‘do nearly anything’ using a cloud computer and connected apps. Dots are always-on AI assistants that OpenAI says can ‘do nearly anything’ using a cloud computer and connected apps. OpenAI is responding to Meta’s buzzy Muse AI with agentic helpers of its own: Dots. During its DevDay keynote on Tuesday, OpenAI announced that Dots will serve as always-on AI assistants that can “do nearly anything” across connected apps in the background while learning your preferences over time. The company’s capable GPT-6 Astra model powers Dots, which use their own cloud computer to access a web browser and more than 4,000 supported apps. You can interact with a Dot through a text-message-like interface that’s similar to the one offered by Muse , as well as hop on a voice call with it from ChatGPT on the web, desktop, or mobile.

sec.title: French Tax Data Theft Using Stolen Staff Passwords Went Undetected for Seven Weeks
sec.brief: An attacker used stolen passwords of staff at France's tax administration to take tax data on hundreds of thousands of taxpayers and businesses in June and July. Neither the tax administration nor France's national cybersecurity agency saw the data leave.
